entities.summary: Otomārs Aleksandrs Oškalns was a prominent Latvian communist and partisan fighter who played a crucial role in the Latvian resistance movement during World War II. Born in Kaive Parish, Latvia, on April 12, 1904, Oškalns joined the Communist Party of Latvia in 1926 and became a key figure in the Latvian Red Army. He participated in several battles against the Soviet occupation and later became a prominent figure in the post-war Latvian government. Oškalns was a vocal advocate for land reform and workers' rights, and his legacy continues to inspire Latvian socialists and communists. His contributions to the country's struggle for independence have been recognized through various awards and honors, including the Latvian Red Army's highest award, the Order of the Red Star. Through his unwavering dedication to the cause, Oškalns left an indelible mark on Latvian history, cementing his place as a hero of the nation's fight for freedom and self-determination.

Otomārs Aleksandrs Oškalns (1904-1947) was a prominent Latvian communist and partisan fighter.


Otomārs Aleksandrs Oškalns was a key figure in the Latvian resistance movement during World War II, playing a crucial role in the country's fight for independence from Soviet occupation. His leadership and bravery inspired a generation of Latvians to take up arms against the Soviet forces.


Oškalns' actions also had significant consequences for the fate of Latvia, contributing to the country's prolonged occupation and the eventual collapse of the Soviet Union. His legacy continues to be felt in Latvia today, with many regarding him as a national hero.


The Latvian resistance movement, in which Oškalns played a central role, was a complex web of organizations and individuals working together to resist Soviet rule. Oškalns' involvement in this movement helped to galvanize the resistance, inspiring others to join the fight for freedom.


Despite his bravery and leadership, Oškalns' life was cut short when he was killed in action in 1947. However, his memory lives on, and he remains an important figure in Latvian history and culture.


Otomārs Aleksandrs Oškalns' story serves as a powerful reminder of the importance of resistance and courage in the face of oppression, and his legacy continues to inspire people around the world.


Otomārs Aleksandrs Oškalns was born in Kaive Parish, Latvia in 1904 and died in 1947.


Otomārs Aleksandrs Oškalns was a member of the Latvian Communist Party.


Otomārs Aleksandrs Oškalns worked closely with other resistance leaders, including the Latvian nationalist, Jānis Kļava.


Otomārs Aleksandrs Oškalns' actions were part of a broader network of partisan groups operating in Latvia during World War II.


Otomārs Aleksandrs Oškalns' story has been documented in various historical accounts, including the Latvian resistance movement's own archives.
